title: 2017 AMC 12A 13
statement: Driving at a constant speed, Sharon usually takes \(180\) minutes to drive from her house to her mother’s house. One day Sharon begins the drive at her usual speed, but after driving \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) of the way, she hits a bad snowstorm and reduces her speed by \(20\) miles per hour. This time the trip takes her a total of \(276\) minutes. How many miles is the drive from Sharon’s house to her mother’s house?

solutions.text:
Let the distance be \(d\) miles and the usual speed \(r\) mph. Since the usual trip is \(3\) hours, \(d=3r.\)

The first \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) of the drive takes \(\dfrac{1}{3}\cdot180=60\) minutes at speed \(r,\) so the remaining \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) takes \(276-60=216\) minutes \(=\dfrac{18}{5}\) hours at speed \(r-20.\)

That final portion covers \(\dfrac{2}{3}d=2r\) miles, so \[ 2r=(r-20)\cdot\dfrac{18}{5}. \] Solving gives \(10r=18r-360,\) so \(r=45\) and \(d=3\cdot45=135.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Her usual drive is \(3\) hours, so the distance equals \(3\) times her usual speed
The final two-thirds takes \(276-\dfrac13\cdot180=216\) minutes at the reduced speed
